prior_importants.description: `removeGateDir` now has to create a new directory before it can delete anything. If the temp filesystem is full (ENOSPC, or EDQUOT for an inode or quota limit), `mkdtempSync` throws. The catch then reports "Could not remove … (ENOSPC); it is left behind." and nothing is freed. Before this change, `rmSync` freed the space in exactly this case. A full temp volume is a realistic way for a gate run to end, for example a runaway test or build writing into scratch. The space is now never reclaimed, so the next `pup merge` fails at its own `mkdtempSync` (`pup-gate-checkout-`, `pup-gate-`) until the operator cleans `$TMPDIR` by hand. The ADR deliberately covers a failed rename, but a failed mkdtemp is a different case and it is not addressed.

findings.description: `movedAside` can still fail with `ENOSPC` on a full volume, so the claim that "a full volume is still freed" (JSDoc L540-541, ADR 0155 L14-16) only holds most of the time. rename(2) is documented to return `ENOSPC` when the directory has no room for the new entry. The new name, `pup-removing-` plus 16 hex, is longer than the names it replaces. If the temp directory's last block has no room for it, the rename has to allocate a block. A regular user cannot get one once only root-reserved space is left, even though plain `unlink` and `rmdir` would still work. `removeGateDir` would then report `Could not remove … (ENOSPC); it is left behind.` and free nothing. This is the round-1 outcome at a lower rate. Either add an in-place fallback, or soften the wording to "needs no new directory".

The comment above `takes a directory gone by the time of the move as removed` says the child removed the directory "between the check and the move". This PR removed that check (the `lstatSync` pre-check in `movedAside`). A missing path now goes straight to `renameSync`'s `ENOENT`, so a reader looks for a check that no longer exists. Suggested wording: "A child granted the directory itself, as an output is, removed it before the move."
